title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1RC1LB, and what is open
description: Proof status of the six-state machine 1RB1RA_1RC1LB_1LD0RA_---0LE_1LC0LF_1RE0LB: what is proved in Lean, what is computed, what is only observed.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape. This page tracks what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

The run's structure is now proved in two layers. Lean has the machine as an explicit map on lists of block lengths, and a theorem that the machine halts exactly when that map's run reaches one specific shape. Read four macro steps at a time, that map is a carry wave running left through the blocks, and Lean now also proves that the halting shape is one arithmetic event: a single number built from the blocks being a power of two. What is open is whether it ever is.
The reduction walks through this link by link; level by level runs the machine in the browser at each level.
verdict: The question is open, and it is now a question about a list map. Lean proves that one macro step of the machine (a phase of transfers, then a sweep to the right or a carry to the left) is an explicit function next on the lists of block lengths, step counts included, and that the machine halts from blank tape iff the macro run reaches a halt. A macro step halts exactly when the head's block is odd and, after the transfers, every block to the left of the head is 2.

Running that map, Lean's kernel proves no halt in the first 2·1010 steps. Lean now also proves the exact machine-step count of each super step (below), so following the super orbit gives longer runs: no halt in the first 1.4·1016 steps, checked by the kernel alone, and no halt in the first 1024 steps with native_decide. In those runs the blocks reach the billions, far from all 2s. What is missing is an argument that the map never produces that shape.

The halting condition in one number, proved. Every fourth time A stands on the blank right of the tape, the tape is blocks p1, …, pm followed by 5, 0, and the next such tape follows from an explicit formula: with dm+1 = 20 and dl = pl + dl+1/2, a wave of halvings runs left while d is even and turns at the first odd d. Lean proves this super step from the macro map for every list, and proves that the machine halts from blank tape iff N = 10 + Σ pl·2m−l (the blocks read as binary digits) is a power of two at some super step of the orbit from (1, 6). The wave reaches the left end when 2m−1 divides N, which explains why the head gets there so rarely (computed, not part of the proof).

claims.title: The machine halts iff N is ever a power of two
claims.text: Let the super orbit start at P = (1, 6) (the tape [1, 6, 5, 0] at step 136) and go on by superstep. The machine halts from blank tape iff some P = (p1, …, pm) of the orbit has N = 10 + Σ pl·2m−l a power of two. Built on halts_iff: the proof follows the macro run, without step counts, from one super step to the next.

claims.title: The super step
claims.text: From the tape [p1, …, pm, 5, 0] (A on the blank right of the last block), the macro run reaches [P′, 5, 0] with P′ = superstep P, or halts. With dm+1 = 20 and dl = pl + dl+1/2, the wave leaves d/2 at each block with d even; at the first odd di the block becomes (di + 5)/2 and the one to its left gains (di − 1)/2. At the left end it goes on halving, and halts when d reaches 1. Proved for every list and every block length, and every tape of the orbit is reached by the machine from blank tape (orbit_tape).

claims.title: The step count of a super step
claims.text: From the tape [p1, …, pm, 5, 0] the machine reaches the next super-step tape in exactly superT steps, or halts right after that many: 200 steps to the first carry of the wave, then 2q2 + q − 5 for each block the wave passes with even d = 2q, then 2q2 + 4q + 17 + A where it turns at an odd d = 2q + 1, with A = 3 plus q + 1 for each block passed. At the left end the wave goes on with p = 0, and a halt there costs 11 steps. Proved for every list by following the timed macro steps of next_sound through the wave. It equals the sum of the four step counts of py/waves.py on 150,000 super steps (a test).

claims.title: When a super step halts
claims.text: A super step halts iff N is a power of two. The wave passes a block exactly when d is even, so if it reaches the left end, 2<sup>m−1</sup>·d<sub>1</sub> = N, and it halts there exactly when d<sub>1</sub> is a power of two; if it turns at an odd d<sub>i</sub>, N is an odd number of at least 3 times a power of two.

claims.title: The machine halts iff the macro run does
claims.text: With X(ls, n, cs) = 0∞ 1lr 0 … 0 1l1 0 A> 1n 000 1c1 00 … 00 1cs 0∞, the run from blank tape is at X([1], 2, []) after 15 steps, and from every X the machine goes where the list function next says, in exactly the steps it says (next_sound). Every reachable X is well formed, so the machine halts from blank tape iff the macro run runM reaches a halt (halts_iff).

claims.title: When a macro step halts
claims.text: A macro step from X(k :: ls, n, cs) halts iff n is odd and every block of (k + ⌊n/2⌋) :: ls equals 2: the carry to the left eats every block of 2 and reaches the left end.

claims.title: Seven block rules
claims.text: Transfer (two cells of the head's block move, one left, one right, 2n + 11 steps), the start and each block of the sweep to the right, and the four stages of the carry to the left; each for every block length and any surrounding tape.

claims.title: No halt in 1.4·10<sup>16</sup> steps
claims.text: The first 107 super steps from [1, 6, 5, 0], with their step counts, are evaluated by Lean's kernel in 1,000 chunks between checkpoints (the checkpoints come from a C program, c/orbitck.c, and are not trusted: every chunk is recomputed). They end after 14,027,148,336,216,160 machine steps without a halt. About 50 minutes on three cores. The macro map, evaluated directly, gives 2·1010 steps (105 macro steps), and step by step the kernel checks 20,000.

claims.title: Two shift rules
claims.text: State A runs right over a block of n ones in n steps; state B runs left over a block of n ones to the 0 before it in n + 1 steps; for every n and any surrounding tape.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>24</sup> steps
claims.text: The super orbit continued to 9.9·1010 super steps by compiled evaluation (native_decide), in 99 chunks after the kernel's 107: more than 1024 machine steps (1,020,655,748,109,356,278,914,592) without a halt. This covers the earlier C run of the wave model to 3.7·1022 steps. With the macro map directly: 9·1013 steps (107 macro steps); step by step: 10,000,000.
claims.where: blank_runs_1e24, lean/OrbitNative.lean, lean/Orbit/N*.lean (check_orbit.sh all, about 1.7 hours on four cores); blank_runs_9e13, lean/MacroRun.lean; blank_runs_10M, lean/Blank.lean

claims.title: The Python macro model
claims.text: py/macro.py computes the same map; it is tested against the reference simulator at every macro configuration of the first 1,000 macro steps (1,322,171 machine steps, the same count Lean's runM_1000 gives) and on built configurations that halt.

claims.title: No simple conserved quantity
claims.text: No quantity a·(number of 1s) + b·(head position) + W[state] is conserved modulo any m from 2 to 12. (The other machine has one modulo 3, which the same search finds.)

claims.title: The wave model's finer events and step counts
claims.text: py/waves.py: each time A stands on the blank right of the tape (four times per super step), the next such time follows from the block lengths by a left-going wave, with exact machine step counts. The super step, the halting criterion and the step count of a whole super step are now proved in Lean; the finer events and their single step counts are not. Checked against tmrun at all 12,927 such times of the first 109 steps, against every new left cell up to 1010 steps, and against the first 2,000 configurations of the proved macro map; Lean's superstep and superT agree with waves.py on its examples.

claims.title: The next return to the left end
claims.text: After step 2,047,931 the head next reaches new tape on the left at step 26,618,972,322, as the wave model predicted; a direct run to 2.7·10<sup>10</sup> steps confirms it and finds no other new left cell in between.

claims.title: Far from the halting shape
claims.text: In 10<sup>7</sup> macro steps the left list of blocks holds blocks in the hundreds of thousands; halting needs every block to the left of the head to be 2.

claims.title: Why the returns to the left end are rare
claims.text: The wave is a binary carry: reaching the left end needs v<sub>2</sub>(N) ≥ m − 1, about once in 2<sup>m−1</sup> super steps if N's low bits behave like coin flips, and each return adds blocks. The observed gaps fit that estimate to within a factor of two. The returns do not stop; they thin out.

claims.title: Almost certainly no halt
claims.text: At a return the deciding number is now about 10<sup>9</sup> and grows; if it behaved like a random integer, the chance of ever hitting a power of two would be far below 10<sup>−6</sup>. N shows no modular obstruction (see below).

claims.title: No invariant keeps N off the powers of two
claims.text: Searched for a property of the orbit that every power of two lacks; none found. For every odd q ≤ 127, N takes every residue a power of two takes mod q, also jointly with N's bit length (2<sup>a</sup> has a + 1 bits). N's popcount and leading bits look like a random number's (it comes within 15 zeros of a power of two). Lower bounds on the blocks cannot help, since halting depends only on the sum N. And the super step started from 3,600 small tapes halts 217 times against about 239 expected if the deciding number were random: the map has no invariant of its own that forbids halting. The one exact pattern found, a four-step cycle 11 → 13 → 14 → 12 of the last block (proved by hand from the super-step formula), only fixes N's parity pattern.

claims.title: Whether it halts
claims.text: Whether N = 10 + Σ pl·2m−l is ever a power of two along the super orbit from (1, 6). By the proved halts_iff_pow2' this is exactly the question whether the machine halts: a Collatz-like question about one orbit.

check: bb6-1RB1RA_1RC1LB/lean/check.sh             # the library, then Machine, Rules, Blank, Macro, MacroRun, Wave, WaveTime (about 2 min)
bb6-1RB1RA_1RC1LB/lean/check_orbit.sh all   # the long runs in parallel (about 3 CPU hours kernel, 6 native)
python3 bb6-1RB1RA_1RC1LB/tests/test_waves.py   # the wave model against direct simulation (about 25 s)
python3 bb6-1RB1RA_1RC1LB/py/n_search.py residues 4000000   # the invariant search (also: digits, starts)
